label: Customers
description: What the registry keeps: one record per customer, identified by their id. The collection is where the record type is written down, so the graphs below name the store and the collection and repeat no shape. It also says what the records may not repeat and what an added column gives the rows already there, so the compiler judges a filter or a patch against the declaration rather than the database finding out at run time.

customers.description: the customers, one row each: no two share an address, a note is a field of the customer, and a row written before the tier column reads as bronze

latest.description: the most recent customer registered into each tier, one row per tier: written in the same transaction as the customer itself, so the two cannot disagree
